data.title: Hook
data.tagline: An automated mechanism that intercepts execution upon specific lifecycle events to run predefined scripts or checks.
data.learningOutcome: You can choose a Hook timing based on events and distinguish how Hooks, Skills, and Plugins are triggered.
data.description: For example, Git can run a check before committing, and some AI tools provide an event after writing a file. The specific event names, parameters, and whether a failure blocks later steps depend on the product. Review the current tool documentation before configuration, and keep dangerous scripts bounded by permissions.

learning.assumes: You know that scripts can run formatting, tests, or other checks locally.
learning.outcome: You can choose a Hook timing based on events and distinguish how Hooks, Skills, and Plugins are triggered.

distinctions.label: Plugin
distinctions.explanation: A Hook executes automatically when a specific lifecycle event fires; a Plugin is a broader module that packages new features or extensions for the host application.

explanation.title: Listen for lifecycle events
explanation.text: A Hook can attach to startup, after a file write, or before a command runs.

explanation.title: Run a preset task
explanation.text: When the event occurs, the tool runs the configured formatter, check, or setup script.

explanation.title: A failure can stop the next action
explanation.text: A pre-commit test hook can block a commit on failure, while running heavy tests after every write can slow the workflow.

data.boundary: A Hook is an event-triggered action, a Skill is an invoked task method, and a Plugin is a distributable package. A Hook can format or check code but cannot repair business logic.

lessonPractice.title: Which mechanism fits automatic formatting after the AI writes a file?

options.label: Configure a post-write Hook to run the formatter after the file-write event
options.feedback: Correct. Hooks are triggered by lifecycle events and run preset tasks after a write completes.

options.label: Create a Skill and let the agent decide whether to format each time
options.feedback: A Skill is an invokable task method, not a listener that automatically responds to a file-write event.

options.label: A Hook will automatically repair business logic bugs in generated code
options.feedback: A Hook only runs its preset script; formatting or checks do not replace logic fixes and review.

data.agentPrompt: Configure a post-write formatting hook for .ts and .tsx files. Explain when it runs and what it changes, and make sure it cannot read secrets or touch unrelated directories.
